angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 123,829,034 km at 211.42 pc = 7.83 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 107315: distance 211.416 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.036), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 211.416 +/- 7.611 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 177.992 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 107315: radius 177.992 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8508.04 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 123,829,034 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4158 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 107315: effective temperature 4158 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.079) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 107315: effective temperature 4158 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.079) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Peg: spectral type K2Ib-II (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Peg: main object type LP*, Long-Period Variable
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps Peg: projected rotation speed 5.6 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)
